question: A developer builds a /fix-issue skill that expects an issue number as input, such as /fix-issue 482. When teammates invoke it without typing a number, they get confused about what to supply. Which frontmatter field should the developer add to SKILL.md so the autocomplete menu shows teammates what to type?
options: A) argument-hint: [issue-number], which displays a placeholder in the autocomplete menu without changing how the skill executes.
B) disable-model-invocation: true, which forces teammates to always type an issue number when invoking the command manually.
C) description: Requires an issue number argument, which Claude reads aloud to the user before executing the skill.
D) arguments: issue-number, which validates that the typed value is numeric before the skill is allowed to run.
correct_answers: A) argument-hint: [issue-number], which displays a placeholder in the autocomplete menu without changing how the skill executes.
explanations: Correct. The argument-hint field is the standard frontmatter key for SKILL.md that provides a placeholder string in the slash‑command autocomplete interface. It helps users understand what input is expected without altering skill execution or validation logic.
Incorrect. disable-model-invocation: true prevents the model from automatically calling the skill, requiring manual invocation. It does not add an input hint or guide the user on what to type.
Incorrect. The description field is shown in the command menu as general help text, but it does not display a placeholder for the argument. It would not appear as a visual hint in the input area.
Incorrect. arguments is not a recognized frontmatter field for SKILL.md. The correct field to provide an argument hint is argument-hint. There is no built‑in numeric validation through frontmatter.
